original_question: Characterize those Frobenius varieties V for which every S in V satisfies the generalized Wilf inequality e_V(S)g(S) <= (e_V(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where e_V(S) denotes the cardinality of the unique minimal V-system of generators of S.
target_in_paper: Section 4 (Frobenius Varieties), the Wilf-type open problem stated after the definition of embedding V-dimension: determine which Frobenius varieties V have the property that every S∈V satisfies e_V(S)g(S) ≤ (e_V(S)−1)(F(S)+1). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the correct open problem in Section 4, keeps the right universal quantifier over all semigroups S in a Frobenius variety V, and uses the same Wilf-type inequality with the V-embedding dimension e_V(S) rather than the ordinary embedding dimension. It also correctly remembers that e_V(S) comes from the unique minimal V-system of generators. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The ambient objects should be defined: a numerical semigroup is a submonoid of ℕ (with ℕ the nonnegative integers) whose complement in ℕ is finite. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The invariants in the inequality should be made explicit: F(S)=max(ℕ∖S) is the Frobenius number, and g(S)=|ℕ∖S| is the genus (the number of gaps). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Frobenius variety needs its full definition: V is a nonempty family of numerical semigroups closed under intersection, and whenever S∈V with S≠ℕ, one also has S∪{F(S)}∈V. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To make e_V(S) fully stand-alone, one should specify that a V-monoid is an intersection of members of V, and that e_V(S) is the cardinality of the unique finite minimal V-system of generators of S viewed as a V-monoid. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The paper phrases the problem as a characterization question for Frobenius varieties themselves, not as proving the inequality for a fixed preselected class beyond that characterization. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Let V be a Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups, that is, a nonempty family V of cofinite submonoids of ℕ such that (i) S,T∈V implies S∩T∈V, and (ii) if S∈V and S≠ℕ, then S∪{F(S)}∈V, where F(S)=max(ℕ∖S). For S∈V, let g(S)=|ℕ∖S|, and let e_V(S) denote the cardinality of the unique minimal V-system of generators of S as a V-monoid (equivalently, of the unique minimal subset A⊆S such that S is the intersection of all V-monoids containing A). Characterize those Frobenius varieties V for which every S∈V satisfies the inequality e_V(S)g(S) ≤ (e_V(S)−1)(F(S)+1). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: This is the exact Section 4 open problem your draft is aiming at: after defining Frobenius varieties, V-monoids, minimal V-systems of generators, and the embedding V-dimension e_V(S), the paper asks for a characterization of those Frobenius varieties for which the Wilf-type inequality holds for every member. Your draft is therefore very close, but it leaves implicit the definitions of numerical semigroup, Frobenius variety, genus, Frobenius number, and the V-monoid meaning behind e_V(S); adding these makes the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper. The nearby discussion does not provide an alternate equivalent reformulation of this specific question, so no paper-backed alternate formulation should be added. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
